newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Cali drug lords' brother sentenced in Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Cali drug lords' brother sentenced in Colombia.

text.p: Jorge Elicer Rodriguez Orejuela, a younger brother of the leaders of Colombia's infamous Cali drug cartel, has been sentenced to 10 years in prison on cocaine trafficking charges, authorities said on Tuesday.

A spokesman for the prosecutor-general's office said the sentence was handed down on Monday by a "faceless" or anonymous judge in Cali, the city in southwest Colombia that gave the criminal drug syndicate its name.

The names of judges handling drug cases in Colombia are kept secret to protect them from hired assassins known as "sicarios", who killed scores of judicial officials on orders from drug lords in the 1980s.

Jorge Elicer is a brother of Gilberto and Miguel Rodriguez Orejuela, the reputed billionaires who were jailed in Bogota last year for heading what U.S. officials have described as the world's largest drug trafficking organisation.

He was found guilty of smuggling two large shipments of cocaine to the United States between 1990 and 1995, but his sentence was reduced from 15 years to 10 because he cooperated with the authorities and confessed to his role in drug running, judicial officials said.

They said Jorge Elicer, who is jailed together with his brothers in the maximum security wing of Bogota's La Picota jail, would serve a total of 14 years in prison, however, because of a previous conviction on illegal weapons charges.
Jorge Elicer was also ordered to pay a $20,000 fine for drug trafficking, the judicial officials said.

Gilberto and Miguel Rodriguez Orejuela, who were arrested in June and August of last year respectively, were the target of an extradition request filed by U.S. Attorney General Janet Reno four months ago. Both have confessed to drug trafficking charges as part of an elaborate plea bargaining agreement but have not yet been sentenced for their crimes.
A judicial official told Reuters their sentences could be handed down anytime within the next few weeks, however.

A Senate panel voted last week to lift the constitutional ban on extradition approved by Colombia's Congress in 1991. The legislation is still a long way from final approval, and it could be modified prior to subsequent votes in the House and Senate.
